title: Sell Mineral Rights in Oakman, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Oakman, AL | Walker County
metaDescription: Own mineral or coalbed methane rights near Oakman, AL? We research the Walker County title first and make a straightforward offer, no pressure to sign.
heroLead: Oakman straddles the Walker and Jefferson county line, sitting squarely inside the coalbed methane fairway that developed across the Black Warrior Basin's core coal seams in the 1980s and 1990s.
intro: By the time large-scale CBM development came through Oakman and the surrounding area, most of the underground coal mining that built this part of Walker County had already wound down, but the same coal seams that had been mined for decades turned out to hold enough methane to support a new round of drilling. That means a lot of families here own a mineral interest that has genuinely been active and paying royalties for twenty, thirty, or more years — which makes the underwriting more straightforward than in areas with no production history at all.

sections.heading: A Real Production History to Work From
paragraphs: If your family has been receiving royalty statements from an Oakman-area CBM unit, that history is the most useful thing you can hand us. We look at how the well or unit has actually performed over time — whether production has been flat, declining, or picked back up with re-completions — rather than guessing based on the county's reputation.

sections.heading: Straddling Two Counties Complicates the Paper Trail
paragraphs: Because Oakman sits near the Walker-Jefferson line, some family holdings here were recorded in one county's courthouse while the mineral interest itself sits partly or entirely in the other. We check both when a tract's exact boundary isn't obvious from the deed, so the offer reflects what's actually owned rather than what a single county's index happens to show.

faqs.question: We've gotten royalty checks for years. Will you honor that history in your offer?
faqs.answer: Yes — a consistent payment history is exactly what we use to price a producing interest. Send us a few recent statements and we'll work from those.

faqs.question: Our land is close to the Walker-Jefferson line. Does that make title harder to confirm?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, since records can sit in either county depending on the original survey. We check both courthouses so nothing gets missed.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests with re-completed or reworked wells?
faqs.answer: Yes. Re-completions often extend a well's productive life, and we factor that into how we look at the unit's recent performance.

faqs.question: Our family owns interests recorded in both Walker and Jefferson county. Can you handle both in one transaction?
faqs.answer: Yes, once we've confirmed each parcel's title in its respective county, we can combine everything into a single offer if that's what your family prefers.
